newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BRAVES ACQUIRE FIRST BASEMAN COLBRUNN FROM TWINS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BRAVES ACQUIRE FIRST BASEMAN COLBRUNN FROM TWINS.

text.p: The Atlanta Braves tried to boost their slumping offense Thursday when they acquired first baseman-outfielder Greg Colbrunn from the Minnesota Twins for a player to be named.
The 28-year-old Colbrunn was batting .281 with five homers and 26 runs batted in for the Twins. He bats right-handed and platooned with Scott Stahoviak at first base.
Colbrunn returns to the National League, where he played for the Montreal Expos and Florida Marlins from 1992-96. He has a career average of .279 with 56 homers and 256 RBI.
"It's a great opportunity," Colbrunn said. "I've been doing my time here with the Twins. They were a great bunch of guys, but now it's time to go and try and help them (Braves) win some ballgames."

The Braves have scored more than four runs just once in their last 13 games. The defending National League champions have not scored more than two runs in any of their last four games, losing three to drop their lead over the second-place Marlins to 4 1/2 games in the National League East.
Colbrunn was batting eighth for the Twins in Thursday afternoon's game at Boston but was removed and told of the trade.

"The big trades have happened already but every so often, like up in Toronto, when Otis (Nixon) gets traded in the first inning, you never know," he said as he left Fenway Park. "You get on a plane and go to that place and play."
Fred McGriff is Atlanta's starting first baseman, but Colbrunn could see time platooning with left fielder Ryan Klesko, who is batting just .247 and struggling against left-handers.
"I'm not sure what my role down there will be, whether it's coming off the bench or getting a start here and there," said Colbrunn.
To replace Colbrunn on the roster, the Twins recalled first baseman-outfielder Brent Brede from Triple-A Salt Lake of the Pacific Coast league.
The 25-year-old Brede batted .279 with seven RBI in two stints for the Twins this season. He was hitting .354 with nine homers and 76 RBI at Salt Lake.
